analysis.title: Quantitative Conviction: An intersection of fundamental conviction and quantitative signals ahead of earnings (Q3 2026, Stocks Reporting W/C 26 Oct)
key_insights: UBS Systematic Advisory pairs fundamental analyst views with quant signals (hedge fund crowding, short interest, retail flow, long-only positioning, ML EPS model, earnings surprise nowcast) for 5 European and 5 US names reporting the week of Oct 26.

Orange (Buy, PT EUR 21.50, reports Oct 27): UBS expects organic resilience across France, Spain, MEA, Poland and Belgium. Guidance has been raised twice YTD. UBS sees scope for management to raise 2028 CMD targets, with UBSe OCF of EUR 5.5bn vs consensus EUR 5.2bn. Quant signals are mixed.

Epiroc (Sell, PT SEK 230, reports Oct 28): UBS forecasts Q3 outcomes of +3%/-3%/-5% vs consensus and expects a mildly negative catalyst. Adjusted EBIT is forecast 5% below consensus due to operating leverage. Orders are above consensus and revenue below. Hedge fund, short-base and ML EPS signals are all bearish.

GSK (Neutral, PT GBX 1,940, reports Oct 28): UBS is cautious on early momentum for Blenrep and Exdensur and sees potential for growth to disappoint at Q3. Exdensur momentum is expected from 4Q26, and Blenrep is on a 'go slow before going big' path because of ocular toxicity management. Quant signals lean buy but without conviction.

Glencore (Buy, PT GBX 690, reports Oct 29): UBS is 19% above consensus on FY26 Marketing EBIT and 25% above on FY27, and sees about 15% upside to consensus 2027 EBITDA at spot commodity prices. Quant signals are the most bullish of the European names (HF x SI and ML EPS both Strong Buy).

Prysmian (Buy, PT EUR 175, reports Oct 29): UBS forecasts 3Q26 adjusted EBITDA of EUR 824m, 5% above consensus, driven by Digital Solutions (repriced data-centre fibre contracts). A possible FY26 EBITDA guidance raise to EUR 2.9-3.0bn from EUR 2.8-2.9bn. The ML EPS signal is a Sell.

Royal Caribbean (Buy, PT USD 367, reports Oct 27): UBS says industry fundamentals are better than feared, with per diems up 24% vs 2019 and supply growth below pre-COVID levels. Quant signals are bearish: HF x Retail Strong Sell, ML EPS Strong Sell (Q1 within SPX), implied move 6.5%.

GE Vernova (Buy, PT USD 1,400, reports Oct 28): UBS stays positive on the multi-year earnings growth outlook. Quant signals split: HF x EN Strong Buy (HF positioning >3std) against ML EPS Strong Sell. Implied move 4.6%.

Microsoft (Buy, PT USD 675, reports Oct 28): UBS (Karl Keirstead) sees a 47% Azure growth bogey and a 46-47% guide as achievable, citing enterprise checks, OpenAI growth, new capacity and hosted-GPU pricing. Copilot usage-based pricing and AI security add M365 upside. Valuation is 23x CY27 non-GAAP EPS. Positioning is tactically bullish and ML EPS is a Sell.

Nextpower (Buy, PT USD 160, reports Oct 28): UBS highlights share capture of 45X advanced manufacturing tax credits and acquisitions that Jon Windham believes have tripled the TAM. Positioning is neutral, ML EPS is a Strong Sell, and the implied move is the largest on the list at 11.6%.

Amazon (Buy, PT USD 318, reports Oct 29): UBS calls it a 'coiled spring' for EPS upside, with incremental capex and opex already in numbers but none of the revenue upside. It trades at 12x EBITDA and 21x P/E. Hedge fund positioning is >3std long, but ML EPS is a Strong Sell.

Across the US names, a recurring pattern is bullish near-term positioning and nowcast signals paired with bearish ML EPS (NTM) signals: GE Vernova, Microsoft, Nextpower and Amazon. Royal Caribbean is bearish on both.

Signal backtests cited: HF x EN gives up to +4.3% excess return over the 60 trading days into earnings. ML EPS long-short earns 5.6% annualised (Sharpe 0.55). HF crowding earns 5.3% annualised (Sharpe 0.83) and crowding momentum 6.9% (Sharpe 0.60). HF x LO earns +8.3% annualised in the US and +5.0% in Europe. HF x Retail earns 12.2% annualised (Sharpe 1.07).

market_movers.rationale: Orange (EU-listed, no US ticker). Organic resilience across units, two guidance raises YTD, possible 2028 CMD target upgrade with UBSe OCF EUR 5.5bn vs consensus EUR 5.2bn.
Epiroc (no US listing). Q3 forecast +3%/-3%/-5% vs consensus, adjusted EBIT 5% below consensus on operating leverage, and manufacturing output too high relative to the scale of the business.
Cautious on initial Blenrep and Exdensur momentum. Exdensur uptake expected from 4Q26, and Blenrep is on a slow launch because of ocular toxicity management.
UBS is 19% above consensus on FY26 Marketing EBIT and 25% above on FY27. Spot commodity prices imply about 15% upside to consensus 2027 EBITDA.
Prysmian (no US ticker given). 3Q26 adjusted EBITDA forecast EUR 824m, 5% above consensus, from Digital Solutions fibre repricing. Possible FY26 guidance raise.
Per diems up 24% vs 2019, supply growth below pre-COVID levels, private island exposure adding demand.
Demand outlook supports multi-year earnings growth that UBS projects.
47% Azure growth bogey and 46-47% guide achievable. Copilot usage-based pricing and AI security add M365 upside. 23x CY27 non-GAAP EPS.
Leading solar hardware provider capturing 45X advanced manufacturing tax credit share. Acquisitions grew TAM 3x per Jon Windham.
Capex and opex are baked into numbers but revenue upside is not. 12x EBITDA and 21x P/E, with a positive revision cycle expected.

sector_views.rationale: Per diems up 24% vs 2019 and supply growth below pre-COVID levels, per UBS on Royal Caribbean.
Thermal and met coal supported by supply disruptions, plus copper and zinc strength. Glencore's commodity basket is up about 20% YTD.
Prysmian forecast 25% EBIT CAGR to 2028 vs about 12% for peers, helped by data-centre fibre repricing.
Epiroc output is too high relative to the scale of the business, with downside risk to margin or cash flow forecasts.

earnings_insights: Orange reports 10/27 (Q3 2026): UBS expects continued strength including a resilient France. UBSe OCF of EUR 5.5bn vs consensus EUR 5.2bn is the number to watch for a potential 2028 CMD target upgrade. Implied move 2.4%, 1.6x the 1M realised average.

Epiroc reports 10/28 (Q3 2026): UBS estimates outcomes of +3%/-3%/-5% vs consensus. Orders are above consensus, revenue is below, adjusted EBIT is 5% below consensus (UBS estimate vs consensus). Implied move 5.1%, 2.6x realised.
GSK reports 10/28 (Q3 2026): UBS sees potential for growth to disappoint on Blenrep and Exdensur launches. Implied move 3.4%, 2.1x realised.
Glencore reports 10/29 (Q3 2026): the key lever is upside in Marketing, with UBS 19% above consensus on FY26 Marketing EBIT and 25% above for FY27. Implied move 2.8%, 1.6x realised.

Prysmian reports 10/29 (Q3 2026): UBS estimate of adjusted EBITDA EUR 824m is 5% above consensus. Digital Solutions organic growth is forecast at 25%, EBITDA EUR 148m, margin 24.7%. UBS is 4%, 10% and 10% above consensus on EBITDA for 2026-28. Implied move 2.4%, 0.9x realised.
Royal Caribbean reports 10/27 (Q3 2026): UBS Earnings Surprise Nowcast sees no material surprise in either direction. Implied move 6.5%, 2.7x realised.
GE Vernova reports 10/28 (Q3 2026): the Earnings Surprise Nowcast shows a strongly positive surprise in one reading (Q5 within SPX) and neutral in another. Implied move 4.6%, 1.8x realised.

Microsoft reports 10/28 (fiscal Q1 2027 per standard calendar): UBS estimate of Azure growth of 47% as the bogey and 46-47% as the guide. Nowcast is a strongly positive surprise (Q5 within SPX). Implied move 4.5%, 3.2x realised.
Amazon reports 10/29 (Q3 2026): Nowcast is strongly positive (Q5 within SPX). Implied move 6.6%, 3.6x realised.
risk_factors: Glencore: commodity price weakness or softer-than-expected marketing earnings.
Epiroc: downside risk to margin or cash flow forecasts from manufacturing output being too high relative to business scale.
GSK: growth from Blenrep and Exdensur launches could disappoint at Q3.
Several US conviction names (GE Vernova, Microsoft, Nextpower, Amazon) have bearish longer-term ML EPS signals despite bullish tactical positioning.
Prysmian shares have been range-bound since de-rating in July and sit on the 200-day moving average.
vol_and_positioning: Implied earnings moves vs 1M realised average: Nextpower 11.6% (3.4x), Amazon 6.6% (3.6x), Royal Caribbean 6.5% (2.7x), Epiroc 5.1% (2.6x), GE Vernova 4.6% (1.8x), Microsoft 4.5% (3.2x), GSK 3.4% (2.1x), Glencore 2.8% (1.6x), Orange 2.4% (1.6x), Prysmian 2.4% (0.9x).
Hedge fund crowding: GE Vernova, Microsoft and Amazon are all >3std long. Glencore is >2std long with a light short base (<2 DTC). Royal Caribbean is >1std short with 5.0 DTC.
Short base: Epiroc has a heavy short base at 10 DTC. Royal Caribbean 5.0 DTC, GSK 4.0 DTC, Orange 3.3 DTC, Prysmian 3.0 DTC, GE Vernova 3.0 DTC, Microsoft 2.5 DTC, Amazon 2.1 DTC.
Long-only positioning: Microsoft and Amazon are underweight among long-only funds, leaving buying capacity into earnings (Buy signal). Orange long-only investors are already overweight.
Retail flows: strong net selling in Microsoft and Glencore, strong net buying in Royal Caribbean, Prysmian and GSK. Flows are muted in Orange and Amazon.

UBS ML EPS model: strongly negative NTM EPS for Royal Caribbean, GE Vernova, Nextpower and Amazon (Strong Sell). Negative for Microsoft, Epiroc and Prysmian (Sell). Strongly positive for Orange and Glencore (Strong Buy), positive for GSK (Buy).
